why_how.text: Work-zone signs generally use an orange background.
Near a construction area, stay alert, slow down, obey the signs and watch for workers and equipment.
Obey instructions from a person directing work-zone traffic with a sign or flag.
Drums, cones and other barriers keep drivers away from closed roads and areas that are dangerous to enter.
Approaching or traveling through a work zone requires readiness for an unexpected stop.
Yield to roadway workers or equipment and keep a cushion of space around them.
Keep a clear gap behind the vehicle ahead in a work zone instead of following too closely.
Speeding in a work zone can result in doubled fines and jail time.

why_how.text: Road markings may take the form of painted lines, arrows, words or symbols.
Pavement markings divide lanes and identify passing permissions, turn lanes, pedestrian paths and stopping points for signs or signals.
White lane lines separate vehicles moving in the same direction and may be solid or dashed.
A solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions.
Do not cross left of double solid yellow centerlines except to turn left or pass a slow-moving vehicle, such as a bicycle or a vehicle showing a slow-moving-vehicle sign.
Beside a solid-and-dashed yellow centerline pair, drivers on the dashed-line side may pass other vehicles.
Beside a solid-and-dashed yellow centerline pair, drivers on the solid-line side may not pass other vehicles.
With a dashed yellow centerline, drivers in either direction may pass vehicles going their way when the maneuver is safe.

Traffic from either direction may enter the shared center lane immediately before turning left, but must not use it for through travel or passing.
A crosswalk identifies the part of the roadway intended for pedestrian crossing.
Yield to pedestrians who are entering a crosswalk or already crossing within it.
Obey a stop line placed before a crosswalk.
Crosswalk markings do not all have the same appearance.
